assessments.reasoning: The pinned SPDX original identifies creatoragent/3_29_0 and marks the ListedLicense deprecation flag false. All six field digests match. The typed identifier and name establish the edition choice, and the comment directly resolves the apparent counterexample presented by the header placeholders.

challenge.method: Compared the generic and positive-feature header digests and tested their competing readings against the generic comment. Held the 1.2-or-later grant fixed while varying the features between one Cover Text, none and unknown. Then varied the starting edition and the authorization.
challenge.results: The headers match byte for byte, yet the generic comment leaves every feature open in all three cases. Unknown features are compatible with this description when the edition grant is established independently. An unavailable notice alone proves neither the grant nor the features. A 1.1-or-later or 1.3-or-later grant has a different starting edition. A published 1.3 can be an option under a 1.2-or-later grant without changing its starting edition. Section 10 excludes an unpublished draft and gives a separate rule for a grant that specifies no version number.

limitations: The identifier leaves the features unspecified even when a work's notice settles them. If the notice is unavailable, the generic identifier itself cannot establish the work's edition grant.

Matching embedded SPDX license bodies do not make the notice choices interchangeable. The SPDX body includes a postal address where the GNU original gives the FSF website, and their line formatting differs. Membership establishes neither textual equivalence to GNU's representation nor authorization for a particular work.
reasoning: The ListedLicense spdxId is http://spdx.org/licenses/GFDL-1.2-or-later and its name is GNU Free Documentation License v1.2 or later. Its comment expressly leaves Invariant Sections, Front-Cover Texts and Back-Cover Texts open. The standard header illustrates later-version wording with three placeholders. The comment correctly names the generic identifier but reverses the suffixes in both feature-specific alternatives.
